description: Experience the quintessential taste of India with our Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken. This recipe brings you succulent chicken marinated in yogurt and aromatic spices, then perfectly charred over a charcoal grill for an unforgettable smoky flavor. It is a true feast for the senses, promising tender, juicy chicken every time.

ingredients.notes: drumsticks and thighs, skin removed and deeply gashed

instructions.title: Prepare the Chicken
instructions.text: Wash the chicken pieces thoroughly and pat them completely dry with paper towels. Make 2-3 deep gashes on each piece to allow the marinade to penetrate deeply.

instructions.title: First Marinade
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine the chicken pieces with 1 tablespoon of lemon juice and 1 teaspoon of salt. Rub well into the gashes. Let it rest for 15 minutes.

instructions.title: Second Marinade
instructions.text: In another bowl, whisk together the thick plain yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, remaining 1 tablespoon lemon juice, tandoori masala, red chili powder, turmeric powder, cumin powder, coriander powder, remaining 0.5 teaspoon salt, and Kashmiri red chili powder (if using). If using mustard oil, add 1 tablespoon to this marinade.

instructions.title: Combine and Marinate
instructions.text: Add the chicken from the first marinade into the second yogurt-spice marinade. Ensure every piece is thoroughly coated. Cover the bowl and refrigerate for a minimum of 6 hours, or preferably overnight, for best flavor.

instructions.title: Prepare the Charcoal Grill
instructions.text: About 30-45 minutes before grilling, light your charcoal. Arrange the hot coals on one side of the grill for indirect heat, or distribute evenly for direct grilling if preferred. The grill should be medium-hot. Clean and oil the grill grates.

instructions.title: Grill the Chicken
instructions.text: Place the marinated chicken pieces directly over medium heat on the oiled grill grates. Cook for 5-7 minutes per side, turning frequently, until the chicken starts to get char marks and cook through.

instructions.title: Basting and Finishing
instructions.text: Once the chicken is mostly cooked, move it to the cooler side of the grill (indirect heat) if needed to finish cooking without burning. Baste generously with melted butter or ghee. Continue grilling, turning and basting occasionally, for another 10-15 minutes, or until the internal temperature reaches 165F (74C) and the chicken is tender and beautifully charred.

instructions.title: Rest and Serve
instructions.text: Remove the chicken from the grill and let it rest for 5 minutes. Garnish with fresh cilantro and serve hot with lemon wedges, mint chutney, and onion rings.

tips: For the most authentic flavor, use full-fat plain yogurt and ensure you drain any excess water to make it thick and creamy for the marinade.
To achieve an even deeper smoky flavor, consider adding a few wood chips (like mesquite or applewood) to your charcoal while grilling.
Always serve Tandoori Chicken immediately after grilling. Pair it with fresh mint chutney, sliced red onions, and a squeeze of fresh lemon juice for a complete experience.
article:
Mastering the art of Indian cuisine at home can seem daunting, but some dishes, while packed with complex flavors, are surprisingly achievable and immensely rewarding. Among these, Tandoori Chicken stands out as a beloved classic, famous for its vibrant red hue, smoky aroma, and succulent texture. While traditional tandoors are not commonplace in home kitchens, the magic of a charcoal grill can perfectly replicate that authentic, flame-licked taste. Get ready to transform your backyard into an Indian culinary haven as we guide you through creating the most delicious Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken, a quintessential Indian dinner recipe.

## What is Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken?

At its heart, Tandoori Chicken is a dish originating from the Indian subcontinent, specifically from the Punjab region. It involves chicken marinated in a mixture of yogurt and a potent blend of spices, then traditionally cooked at high heat in a clay oven called a tandoor. The tandoor's unique design imparts a distinct smoky flavor and ensures the chicken is cooked through while remaining incredibly moist. When we talk about Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken, we're aiming to capture that same smoky essence and high-heat cooking using a standard charcoal grill. The yogurt marinade tenderizes the meat, while the spices create a complex flavor profile that is tangy, spicy, and deeply aromatic. The direct heat from the charcoal sears the chicken, locking in juices and developing those coveted charred bits that are a hallmark of this iconic Indian dinner recipe.

## Ingredients You Need for Tandoori Chicken

Creating authentic Tandoori Chicken begins with selecting the right ingredients. Here’s what you'll need for this flavorful Indian dinner recipe:

For the Chicken:
*   1 whole chicken (about 3-4 lbs), cut into 8 pieces (or 6-8 chicken thighs/drumsticks), skin removed and deeply scored.

For the First Marinade:
*   2 tablespoons lemon juice
*   1 teaspoon salt
*   1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste

For the Second Marinade:
*   1 cup thick Greek yogurt (or hung curd)
*   2 tablespoons ginger-garlic paste
*   1 teaspoon red chili powder (adjust to taste, Kashmiri chili powder for color)
*   1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder
*   1 teaspoon ground cumin
*   1 teaspoon ground coriander
*   1 teaspoon garam masala
*   1 teaspoon tandoori masala (optional, but enhances flavor)
*   1 teaspoon kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves), crushed
*   1/2 teaspoon black salt (kala namak, optional for authentic tang)
*   1/4 teaspoon red food color (optional, for classic vibrant red, or use beetroot powder/paprika for natural color)
*   2 tablespoons mustard oil (or any neutral oil)

For Grilling:
*   Plenty of charcoal
*   Lighter fluid or a chimney starter
*   Oil for greasing the grill grates

## Step-by-Step Instructions for Grilling

Making delicious Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken is a process that rewards patience and attention to detail. Follow these steps for a perfect result:

1.  **Prepare the Chicken:** Wash the chicken pieces thoroughly and pat them completely dry with paper towels. Using a sharp knife, make deep slits or scores on the chicken pieces, especially on the thicker parts. This allows the marinade to penetrate deeply and helps the chicken cook more evenly.

2.  **First Marinade:** In a large bowl, combine the lemon juice, salt, and ginger-garlic paste. Rub this mixture all over the scored chicken pieces, ensuring it gets into the slits. Let it marinate for at least 15-20 minutes at room temperature. This initial acidic marinade helps tenderize the chicken and kickstarts the flavor infusion.

3.  **Second Marinade:** In a separate bowl, whisk together the Greek yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, red chili powder, turmeric, cumin, coriander, garam masala, tandoori masala (if using), crushed kasuri methi, black salt (if using), and red food color (if using). Stir in the mustard oil until everything is well combined into a thick, vibrant paste.

4.  **Combine Marinades:** Add the chicken from the first marinade into the second marinade bowl. Ensure every piece of chicken is thoroughly coated with the yogurt-spice mixture. Cover the bowl and refrigerate for a minimum of 4 hours, but ideally overnight (12-24 hours) for the best flavor and tenderness. The longer the marination, the more flavorful and moist your Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken will be.

5.  **Prepare the Grill:** About 30-45 minutes before you plan to cook, prepare your charcoal grill. Arrange the charcoal in a single layer for even, direct heat. Light the charcoal using a chimney starter or lighter fluid, and let it burn until it's covered with a layer of white ash, indicating medium-high heat. Clean your grill grates thoroughly with a wire brush and lightly oil them to prevent sticking.

6.  **Grill the Chicken:** Remove the chicken from the refrigerator about 30 minutes before grilling to bring it closer to room temperature. Place the marinated chicken pieces directly over the hot charcoal. Avoid overcrowding the grill, as this can lower the temperature and steam the chicken instead of grilling it.

7.  **Cook and Turn:** Grill the chicken for about 5-7 minutes per side, turning frequently to ensure even cooking and prevent burning. You want to achieve a beautiful char on the outside while cooking the chicken through. The total grilling time will vary depending on the size of your chicken pieces and the heat of your grill, but typically ranges from 20-30 minutes. The internal temperature of the thickest part of the chicken should reach 165°F (74°C).

8.  **Final Touches:** During the last few minutes of grilling, you can optionally baste the chicken with a little melted butter or oil for extra richness and shine. Once cooked, remove the Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken from the grill and let it rest for 5-10 minutes before serving.

## Pro Tips for the Best Results

*   **Marination is Non-Negotiable:** The longer you marinate, the more flavor and tenderness you'll achieve. Overnight is truly best for this Indian dinner recipe.
*   **Thick Yogurt is Key:** Using Greek yogurt or hung curd (yogurt drained of excess whey) prevents the marinade from becoming watery, ensuring it clings to the chicken.
*   **Score Deeply:** Don't be shy with scoring the chicken. Deeper cuts mean more surface area for the marinade to penetrate.
*   **Maintain Grill Heat:** While you want high heat to start, be prepared to move chicken to cooler spots or adjust vents to prevent excessive charring and burning, especially for thicker pieces.
*   **Don't Overcrowd:** Give each piece of chicken space on the grill for optimal browning and even cooking.
*   **Resting is Essential:** Just like with any grilled meat, letting the Tandoori Chicken rest allows the juices to redistribute, resulting in a more succulent bite.
*   **Flavor Boost:** For an extra layer of smokiness, consider adding a few wood chips (like apple or hickory) to your charcoal fire during the last 10 minutes of grilling.

## Serving Suggestions

Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken is a feast for the senses on its own, but it truly shines when served with traditional accompaniments. Garnish generously with fresh cilantro leaves, a sprinkle of chaat masala, and plenty of lemon wedges for squeezing over the hot chicken. It pairs perfectly with warm, fluffy naan bread or roti to scoop up the flavorful juices. A cooling mint-coriander chutney or a refreshing raita (yogurt dip with cucumber and spices) provides a wonderful contrast to the spicy chicken. For a complete Indian dinner recipe, serve alongside basmati rice or a simple kachumber salad (diced cucumber, tomato, onion with lemon and spices).

## Variations and Substitutions

While the classic Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken is a masterpiece, there are many ways to adapt this Indian dinner recipe to your taste or dietary needs:

*   **Vegetarian Options:** The same marinade can be used for paneer tikka, mushroom tikka, or mixed vegetable skewers. Marinate paneer cubes for 1-2 hours and grill until lightly charred.
*   **Other Proteins:** Try the marinade on fish fillets (marinate for only 30-60 minutes) or even lamb chops for a different twist.
*   **Spice Level:** Adjust the amount of red chili powder to your preference. For a milder version, reduce chili powder and add more paprika for color. For more heat, add a pinch of cayenne pepper.
*   **Natural Color:** If you prefer to avoid food coloring, a blend of Kashmiri chili powder (for vibrant red, less heat) and a touch of beetroot powder can give a beautiful natural hue.
*   **Alternative Cooking Methods:** While the smoky flavor of Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken is unparalleled, you can bake it in a hot oven (400°F/200°C) or cook it in an air fryer for a similar taste, though it will lack the distinct char and smoke.

Embrace the sizzle and smoke of your charcoal grill to bring this incredible Indian dinner recipe to life. The effort of marinating and grilling will be richly rewarded with flavorful, tender, and beautifully charred Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken that will impress family and friends alike. Enjoy the journey of creating this iconic dish right in your own backyard!
